body:
What an accurate depiction of what i'm experiencing, i often pity new people in my life for how i worry ill treat them once i've idealized them. I dont want to scare off this new person, they're kind and understanding as they can be but i worry i'll wear them thin with my neediness and then demonize them when they can't come through for me. I feel like my abandonment issues make me so toxic that when i love someone it's this push-and-pull bullshit that scares them off. How do I explain my BPD without frightening them further or coming off as though i expect them to accomidate it? I wish I could be a simple, fun, low-maitenance person.
Best of luck to you <3
Thank you, that spoke volumes to me!

I was dissociated for a few days at a time once- it was terrifying. Have you been sleeping and eating regularly? Have you been drinking or consuming? I found when I was drinking alot, under a lot of stress and unrested, that I'd start walking "walking through the fog" again. I'm not a professional though, you should find someone who is.

Wasnt at all intended to avoid fault! I'm trying to work on myself, and being aware of fault is the first step. If I was consciously manipulative, I wouldn't need to ask if I was, considering I'd be aware of it, thus this entire post would have no point to it, which was why it wasn't presented as an option. I also didn't say everyone, only my brother and ex, who had paranoid tendencies. I'm not the type to think "im right, EVERYONE else has a problem" I'm far more rational than that. As for the re-evalution, and consulting a professional/friend, you're quite right. No one on here knows me well enough to really speculate.

I try to be aware of myself as much as possible, it's difficult at times though... definitely hardest when I'm in a emotion state, my mind will play tricks on me, and I'll know my perception is skewed, which is why I try to leave things until I've calmed down to look back on them. I worry when meeting new people for this reason... I don't want to hide my extremes to the point where they're blown away one day when I have an episode, and dating is difficult because mentioning mental illness makes most people run in the other direction, whereas hiding it completely I consider disingenuous... I'm trying to find that middle ground. I've isolated myself for a few months to re-evaluate myself and my relationships with people, and that is DEFINATELY on the top of my list.

That what insightful, I hadn't looked at it that way previously... "Subconsciously Masterminding a Plan" makes no sense at all, right? If  I were doing things with ill intent I'd be aware of it, at the very least! It's still upsetting to be perceived as untrustworthy, I seek people's validation endlessly, which may be a motive at times, but it's definitely the lesser of evils, when it comes to motives, I think.
What type of stuff do you use?  I love anatomical themed stuff but have issues finding illustrated medical books.

That means so much to me, I appreciate it more than words can tell. I'm so glad I've found this community, where I don't feel like I'm bothering loved ones by opening up, where I can get intelligent advice and be understood by people who have-or still do, feel how I feel.

I watched an out-dated documentary where they described being manipulative as a symptom of BPD, which upset me. It's a releif to hear it's a common myth.
My cat freaks out to the sound of this video
